name: Urothelial cell (umbrella cell)
short_description: Large, dome-shaped surface cell of the bladder's transitional epithelium (urothelium). Its apical membrane is armored with rigid uroplakin plaques and can unfold via a reserve pool of fusiform vesicles as the bladder fills, while tight junctions and a glycosaminoglycan coat seal it against acidic, hypertonic urine.

textbook.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; broad dome-shaped/cuboidal cell (not tall/columnar, not round), apical scalloped cobblestone mosaic of uroplakin plaques with hinge lines instead of a brush border, two violet nuclei, dense cluster of small pale blue-grey fusiform vesicles just under the apical membrane, teal tight-junction band, gold cytokeratin filament bundles, orange-red mitochondria, teal-green Golgi stack, lavender rough ER, muted dusty textbook palette, thin outlines, dark charcoal background, no border, no text)

sem.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; single specimen, warm sandy-tan false colour, true 3D surface texture of raised polygonal plaque facets separated by fine hinge-line grooves - a scalloped/crazy-paving mosaic, not a villous microvilli fringe; no internal organelles as expected for SEM; dark uncluttered background; no border, no text)
